# The Blue Reel

<!-- Prose word count excluding the heading: approximately 1,000, manually estimated. -->

All afternoon, Nia had been looking for a reason to knock on the blue gate next door. June had moved to Willow Lane two weeks ago. She waved when the grown-ups were watching, then disappeared whenever the children started a game. Nia wanted to fly her new kite with someone, not just show it off. She also wanted June to feel that the village had room for her.

The kite waited on the kitchen table, white paper stretched over two bamboo spars. Nia carried it to Tomas’s village kite workshop. Red and gold kites filled the rafters, and a blue wooden reel sat beside the door. Tomas was oiling a pair of scissors. “May I borrow that reel for the afternoon?” Nia asked. “The string on mine is almost gone.”

Tomas tested the reel’s handle with his thumb. “It’s my father’s. The line is strong, but it catches if you yank it. Bring it back wound neatly.” Nia promised. The reel was heavier than she expected. “Are you taking the big kite to the common?” Tomas asked. “I’m asking June to come.” “Good,” he said. “Ask her, don’t decide for her.”

June opened the gate only a hand’s width. “I’ve never flown a kite,” she said. Nia nearly answered that it was easy, then stopped. “You can choose when we let it go. We can stay away from the crowd.” June looked toward the busy green. “Just us?” Nia nodded. After a moment, June stepped out and shut the gate behind her.

At the workshop bench, June held the kite while Nia checked its frame. One spar had a fine split. The reel had enough line to lash the crack, but using it meant spending a little of what Tomas had lent. Nia hesitated. June touched the paper beside the spar, not the split itself. “It might hold if we tie it gently.”

Nia used three careful turns of string around the bamboo. The knot stayed put. They added a tail from blue cloth and checked that the paper did not sag. June asked if she could draw a small mark on the kite. Nia passed her the pencil. June made a neat blue star near the lower corner, then smiled at how little space it took.

Before leaving, June tied a loose ribbon to the workshop’s weather pole. It streamed out, then drooped, then streamed again. “The wind is changing,” she said. Nia had been thinking only about whether there would be wind at all. She listened to the ribbon, and the two of them carried the kite toward the common, taking the open path along the bakery wall.

The grass was still damp from morning rain. Nia held the reel; June held the tail. At Nia’s count, they ran. The kite lifted above the grass. A gust tugged the borrowed line sideways, and it looped over a low hawthorn twig. The kite hung crooked. June caught its tail before it dragged, while Nia felt the handle pull hard against her palms.

Nia could jerk the reel and try to wrench the line loose. It might save the kite quickly, but the string could snap—or the wooden handle could break. She remembered Tomas’s warning. June’s fingers were trembling on the tail, though she hadn’t let go. “Tell me what you need,” Nia said, instead of ordering her to run.

“Give me the handle,” June said. “Not all of it. Let me feel the pull.” Nia passed her the reel and took the kite’s tail. June waited for the ribbon’s lull, then fed out a little slack. Nia eased the twig free. Neither pulled alone. The kite dipped to the grass, with its frame intact and the line still whole.

They could have packed up. Instead, June looked at the ribbon and counted the breaths between its flutters. “Now,” she said. They ran together. June kept the reel steady while Nia guided the kite into the air. This time it climbed above the hawthorn and held. The blue star flashed when the kite turned. June’s laugh came out before she could hide it.

When the gusts grew stronger, they brought the kite down carefully. Nia wound in the loose string; June kept the tail from tangling around their ankles. They carried the reel back to Tomas’s workshop. “Every turn is neat,” he said, inspecting it. Nia explained how they had used a short length to mend the spar. Tomas examined the knot and nodded. “That’s what borrowed things are for, if you look after them.”

June wrote her name beneath the blue star. Nia added hers beside it. They hung the kite in the workshop window, where the afternoon light shone through its paper. June was still quiet when the village children passed, but now she stood beside Nia, holding the pencil. The kite had flown because they had trusted each other with its two ends—and the reel was back where it belonged.

'''Scene-local prose, conditioned on committed world state.'''


def render(scene_id, params, before, after):
    if scene_id == 'workshop':
        return ('Nia wanted June, the new girl on Willow Lane, to fly a kite with her—not watch from behind the gate. '
                'At Tomas’s village workshop she pointed to the blue string reel. “May I borrow it for the afternoon?” '
                'Tomas turned its wooden handle. “Bring it back wound tight; it was my father’s.” '
                'Nia promised, and carried it out carefully.')

    if scene_id == 'invite':
        if after['neighbor.comfort'] == 'quiet':
            return ('June kept one shoulder behind the gate. “I don’t know how to fly one,” she said. '
                    'Nia resisted saying it was easy. “You can choose when we let it go. We can stay away from the crowd.” '
                    'June studied the blue reel. “Just us?” Nia nodded. June opened the gate, still holding her sleeve.')
        return ('June opened the gate. “I’ve never flown a kite,” she said. Nia admitted that her first one had landed '
                'in a cabbage patch. June laughed, then glanced at the children gathering on the green. “I don’t like '
                'everyone watching.” “Then we’ll have our own bit of sky,” Nia said. June stepped out beside her.')

    if scene_id == 'vignette_mark':
        return ('By the lane, June asked to draw on the kite. Nia handed her the pencil instead of choosing for her. '
                'June made one small blue star near the corner. “My brother said a mark helps you find your own kite,” '
                'she said. Nia liked the star. It made the plain paper feel shared already.')

    if scene_id == 'prepare_kite':
        if after['kite.repaired']:
            return ('At the bench, June found a split spar. Nia used three careful turns from the borrowed reel to lash it; '
                    'the knot held. They tied on a balanced tail, though the repair spent some of their line. '
                    '“A mend, not a miracle,” June said, carrying the kite out with Nia.')
        if after['kite.frame_ok']:
            return ('At the bench, June held the frame while Nia checked each bamboo spar. Nothing had split, so they '
                    'tied on a tail weighted for the day’s breeze and kept the reel’s line free. “Ready?” Nia asked. '
                    'June tested the knot with a gentle tug. “Ready enough to try.” They carried the kite out together.')
        return ('At the bench, June found a split spar. The reel was too short to lash it safely, so Nia fitted the tail '
                'without pretending the frame was sound. “We can try gently,” she said. June held the kite level, not by '
                'its weak corner. They carried it out together.')

    if scene_id == 'vignette_ribbon':
        if after['wind.vane'] == 'gusty':
            return ('Before they left, June tied a ribbon to the weather pole. It streamed, sagged, then snapped straight '
                    'again. “The wind keeps changing its mind,” she said. Nia had been watching the kites overhead, not '
                    'the gaps between gusts. They agreed to wait for June’s count before choosing a moment to run.')
        return ('Before they left, June tied a ribbon to the weather pole. It streamed steadily. “Not much of a gust,” '
                'she said. Nia had been watching the kites overhead, not the air at their hands. June smiled at the '
                'ribbon. “I can tell you when it changes.” Nia gave her the loose end to carry.')

    if scene_id == 'walk_to_commons':
        return ('They carried the kite and reel along the bakery wall to the open common. June stayed beside Nia, not '
                'behind her, and held the kite away from the damp hedge. The green was busy at its far end, so they '
                'chose the quiet patch near the hawthorn. “This is our bit of sky,” Nia said. June nodded.')

    if scene_id == 'first_flight':
        if after['kite.tangled']:
            return ('The kite lifted over the grass, then a sharp gust drove its line into a low hawthorn twig. June '
                    'caught the tail before it tore free. Nia let the borrowed reel run instead of yanking; the kite '
                    'hung crooked, trembling just above the hedge.')
        if after['kite.initial_lift']:
            return ('On Nia’s count, the kite rose above the grass. Borrowed line slid through the reel, and June kept '
                    'one hand at the tail. It climbed only as high as the hedge before the wind faltered, but it had '
                    'flown. Then the line quivered in Nia’s palm.')
        return ('The kite hopped once and nosed into the grass. The borrowed line kept it from skittering away. June '
                'picked up the tail, careful not to touch the weak spar. “It tried,” Nia said. A gust rattled the hedge; '
                'neither child blamed the other for the drop.')

    if scene_id == 'response':
        if before['kite.tangled']:
            opening = ('The gust had looped line around a low hawthorn twig. June held the tail while Nia fed slack '
                       'from the reel, and together they eased it free. ')
        else:
            opening = 'They checked the clear line together, watching the gust rather than fighting it. '
        if after['neighbor.role'] == 'reel':
            body = ('Nia offered June the handle. June’s fingers shook, but she took it and called each lull; Nia '
                    'steadied the tail. They waited for June’s count before deciding how high to try.')
        else:
            body = ('June was not ready to hold the reel. Nia offered her the tail and let her choose the release. '
                    '“Wait—now,” June said. Nia kept the handle steady. They would not yank the line just to prove '
                    'the kite could fly.')
        return opening + body

    if scene_id == 'ending_flight':
        if before['neighbor.role'] == 'reel':
            control = 'June guided the handle while Nia steadied the kite’s tail. '
        else:
            control = 'June called the lull while Nia let the reel run. '
        if before['kite.mark']:
            mark = 'They signed beside June’s blue star and set the kite on the workshop rack.'
        else:
            mark = 'They signed their kite and set it on the workshop rack.'
        return ('On the second run, the kite rose above the hawthorn and held. ' + control +
                'They brought it down before the gusts returned, rewound the loose line, and carried it back to Tomas. '
                'He took his borrowed reel with a nod. ' + mark + ' The blue paper turned in the afternoon light.')

    if scene_id == 'ending_grounded':
        if before['kite.height'] == 'low':
            first = 'The kite had climbed above the grass before the gust pulled it back. '
        else:
            first = 'The kite had only hopped across the grass. '
        mark = 'June’s blue star showed between their names. ' if before['kite.mark'] else ''
        return (first + 'June asked them not to pull harder. Nia listened. They folded the kite carefully; '
                'the borrowed reel had kept it from escaping and brought the loose line home. Tomas took back his '
                'wound spool. ' + mark + 'The girls signed the paper and hung it in the workshop window, '
                'where the afternoon light found it.')

    raise ValueError(f'No prose for scene: {scene_id}')

from copy import deepcopy
from dataclasses import asdict
import unittest

from storyscenes.mini_adventures.local_play import LocalPlay
from storyscenes.runtime import StoryError
from .world import (
    Parameters, SCENES, generate, guard, initial, parameters, play_scene, replay, validate,
)


class KiteWorldTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def normalized(self, episodes):
        return [
            {'id': episode.id, 'before': episode.before, 'after': episode.after,
             'events': list(episode.events), 'text': episode.text}
            for episode in episodes
        ]

    def audit_row(self, row):
        p = Parameters(**row['parameters'])
        episodes = replay(p, row['path'])
        self.assertEqual(self.normalized(episodes), row['episodes'])
        self.assertEqual([episode.id for episode in episodes], row['path'])
        self.assertEqual(row['story'], '\n\n'.join(episode.text for episode in episodes))
        self.assertEqual(episodes[-1].after, row['final_state'])
        self.assertTrue(row['final_state']['story.ended'])
        self.assertTrue(row['final_state']['story.outcome'])
        state = initial(p)
        for episode in episodes:
            self.assertEqual(episode.before, state)
            self.assertTrue(guard(episode.id, state))
            self.assertTrue(episode.events)
            self.assertGreaterEqual(len(episode.text.split()), 40)
            self.assertLessEqual(len(episode.text.split()), 70)
            for event in episode.events:
                for key, value in event['requires'].items():
                    self.assertEqual(state[key], value)
                self.assertTrue(event['changes'])
                for key, change in event['changes'].items():
                    self.assertEqual(state[key], change['before'])
                    self.assertNotEqual(change['before'], change['after'])
                    state[key] = change['after']
                validate(state)
            self.assertEqual(state, episode.after)
        return row

    def test_both_lengths_over_one_hundred_seeds_and_exact_replay(self):
        outcomes = set()
        for seed in range(100):
            for count in (7, 8):
                row = self.audit_row(generate(seed, count=count))
                self.assertEqual(row['scene_count'], count)
                self.assertEqual(len(row['path']), count)
                self.assertEqual(len(row['path']), len(set(row['path'])))
                self.assertIn(row['path'][-1], {'ending_flight', 'ending_grounded'})
                outcomes.add(row['final_state']['story.outcome'])
        self.assertEqual(outcomes, {'shared_flight', 'shared_grounded_kite'})

    def test_parameter_validation_and_seed_determinism(self):
        self.assertEqual(parameters(2026102401), parameters(2026102401))
        invalid = (
            {'wind': True}, {'gust': 5}, {'reel_length': 11},
            {'frame_sound': 1}, {'tail_weight': 0}, {'shyness': 5},
        )
        for values in invalid:
            with self.subTest(values=values), self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                Parameters(**values)
        for count in (True, 6, 9):
            with self.subTest(count=count), self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                generate(count=count)

    def test_failed_scene_and_failed_local_action_do_not_mutate_caller(self):
        p = Parameters()
        state = initial(p)
        saved = deepcopy(state)
        with self.assertRaises(StoryError):
            play_scene(p, state, 'ending_flight')
        self.assertEqual(state, saved)

        play = LocalPlay(state, actors=('Nia',), validate=validate)
        play_state, play_events = deepcopy(play.state), deepcopy(play.events)
        with self.assertRaises(StoryError):
            play.act('borrow_without_a_guard', {'reel.borrowed': True}, **{'story.phase': 'broken'})
        self.assertEqual(play.state, play_state)
        self.assertEqual(play.events, play_events)

    def test_optional_vignettes_are_optional_and_not_run_offstage(self):
        seven = generate(12, count=7)
        eight = generate(12, count=8)
        vignettes = {'vignette_mark', 'vignette_ribbon'}
        self.assertFalse(vignettes.intersection(seven['path']))
        self.assertEqual(len(vignettes.intersection(eight['path'])), 1)

        p = Parameters()
        plain_path = ('workshop', 'invite', 'prepare_kite', 'walk_to_commons',
                      'first_flight', 'response', 'ending_grounded')
        plain = replay(p, plain_path)[-1].after
        self.assertFalse(plain['story.mark_seen'])
        self.assertFalse(plain['wind.observed'])
        self.assertEqual(plain['kite.mark'], '')

    def test_borrowed_reel_location_and_string_are_continuous(self):
        p = Parameters(wind=3, gust=1, reel_length=32, frame_sound=False,
                       tail_weight=2, shyness=2)
        row = generate(6, count=8, params=p)
        state = initial(p)
        for episode in replay(p, row['path']):
            for event in episode.events:
                for key, change in event['changes'].items():
                    state[key] = change['after']
                validate(state)
        final = row['final_state']
        self.assertEqual(final['reel.owner'], 'Tomas')
        self.assertEqual(final['reel.location'], 'workshop')
        self.assertFalse(final['reel.borrowed'])
        self.assertTrue(final['reel.used_for_flight'])
        self.assertEqual(final['reel.line_out'], 0)
        self.assertEqual(final['reel.remaining'] + final['reel.patch_used'], final['reel.length'])
        self.assertEqual(final['neighbor.location'], 'workshop')

    def test_paired_counterfactuals_change_ending_and_agency(self):
        p = Parameters(wind=3, gust=1, reel_length=32, frame_sound=True,
                       tail_weight=2, shyness=4)
        with_mark = ('workshop', 'invite', 'vignette_mark', 'prepare_kite',
                     'walk_to_commons', 'first_flight', 'response', 'ending_flight')
        without_mark = ('workshop', 'invite', 'prepare_kite', 'walk_to_commons',
                        'first_flight', 'response', 'ending_grounded')
        marked = replay(p, with_mark)[-1].after
        unmarked = replay(p, without_mark)[-1].after
        self.assertEqual(marked['story.outcome'], 'shared_flight')
        self.assertEqual(unmarked['story.outcome'], 'shared_grounded_kite')
        self.assertEqual(marked['neighbor.role'], 'reel')
        self.assertEqual(unmarked['neighbor.role'], 'tail')

        good_weather = Parameters(wind=3, gust=1, reel_length=32, frame_sound=True,
                                  tail_weight=2, shyness=2)
        bad_weather = Parameters(wind=5, gust=1, reel_length=32, frame_sound=True,
                                 tail_weight=2, shyness=2)
        self.assertEqual(generate(9, count=7, params=good_weather)['final_state']['story.outcome'], 'shared_flight')
        self.assertEqual(generate(9, count=7, params=bad_weather)['final_state']['story.outcome'], 'shared_grounded_kite')

    def test_generated_inventory_mapping_is_complete(self):

# The Blue Reel: runnable mini-adventure

This pack uses only the Python standard library and the supplied `LocalPlay` / runtime. It makes no network or API calls. Run commands from the repository root, where `storyscenes` is importable.

## Run and replay

```bash
python -m storyscenes.mini_adventures.kite.world --seed 0 --scenes 8
python -m storyscenes.mini_adventures.kite.world --seed 0 --scenes 7
python -m unittest storyscenes.mini_adventures.kite.test_world
python check_pack.py .
```

The module prints the generated prose. `generate(seed, count=7 or 8, params=...)` returns the JSON-native path, event traces, state snapshots, and final state. `replay(params, path)` returns the same episodes for any compatible path. Seeded parameters are reproducible; scene search is bounded and speculative episodes are detached from committed state.

`Parameters` has six validated, consequential fields:

- `wind`: 1–5; the usable flying range is 2–4.
- `gust`: 0–4; stronger gusts can snag the first lift and prevent a safe second run.
- `reel_length`: 12–45 metres; short line can prevent a repair or a sustained flight.
- `frame_sound`: whether the bamboo spar starts sound. A repair consumes three metres of the borrowed reel when enough line is available.
- `tail_weight`: 1–4; only a balanced tail (2 or 3) is stable in this small model.
- `shyness`: 1–4; this changes the invitation and whether June first takes the reel or the tail.

## Explicit ending recipes

Use a JSON file to override the seeded values. The omitted CLI defaults are filled from the seed, but these examples set every parameter explicitly.

```bash
printf '%s\n' '{"wind":3,"gust":1,"reel_length":32,"frame_sound":true,"tail_weight":2,"shyness":2}' > /tmp/kite-flight.json
python -m storyscenes.mini_adventures.kite.world --seed 0 --scenes 7 --params /tmp/kite-flight.json
```

That recipe makes `ending_flight` possible: the frame, tail, line, and wind are suitable, and June is comfortable taking the reel. The optional ribbon vignette is not required.

```bash
printf '%s\n' '{"wind":5,"gust":1,"reel_length":32,"frame_sound":true,"tail_weight":2,"shyness":2}' > /tmp/kite-grounded.json
python -m storyscenes.mini_adventures.kite.world --seed 0 --scenes 8 --params /tmp/kite-grounded.json
```

That recipe ends at `ending_grounded`, because a wind strength of 5 is outside the safe flying range. The kite is folded, signed, displayed in the workshop window, and the borrowed reel is returned; the ending is complete rather than a promise to try later. Either recipe works at both supported lengths. An eight-scene route includes exactly one of the two optional vignettes; a seven-scene route includes neither.

## Design and limitations

The seven required encounters are borrowing, inviting, preparing, walking to the common, first lift, responding, and a compatible ending. `vignette_mark` and `vignette_ribbon` are separate, optional encounters. Neither is simulated when omitted. The inventory maps about twenty reference beats to executable scenes and explains consolidated actions.

The ending depends on the enacted frame, string, wind, tail, and local choice. The reel pays out line, may supply a repair, is rewound, and is returned to Tomas. June has agency in either ending: she may handle the reel or choose and hold the tail. The grounded outcome does not claim the kite flew.

This is a small scenario model, not a general kite or weather simulator. It has two terminal outcomes, fixed characters, no repeated scenes, and a deliberately narrow physical state. The reference story is an authored example, not a requirement that every generated route repeat its exact events. Prose is composed per scene from local state; it is not a prewritten whole-story variant system. Mechanical tests do not establish literary quality.
